children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to know about the children you're claiming for. 

**What is your child's age (or the age of each child if you have more than one)?**

This will help me determine which rules apply to your situation. The key age groups are:
- **Under 16** - automatically qualifying
- **16-19 years old** - need to check if they're in education or training
- **20 years or over** - not eligible for Child Benefit

Please tell me the name and age of each child you'd like me to assess.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'd like to check if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 17.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So we're assessing eligibility for **Alex, who is 17 years old**.

Since Alex is in the 16-19 age group, I need to check whether they're in qualifying education or training. This is an important requirement for children aged 16-19 to be eligible for Child Benefit.

**Is Alex currently in any of the following:**
1. Full-time education (at school, college, or university)?
2. An apprenticeship?
3. Participating in a government-approved training course?

Or has Alex left education/training and is now working or not in any of these activities?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex left school and isn't in any education or training at the moment. They're working full-time now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Let me navigate to the next step based on Alex's situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. So Alex is no longer in education or training and is working full-time. However, there's an important rule to check: **if Alex left education or training recently (within a certain timeframe), there may still be an extension period where they could qualify**.

**When did Alex leave school?** Specifically:
- Was it within the last 20 weeks?
- Or was it longer ago than that?

This is important because if Alex left education recently, they may still be eligible for Child Benefit during a transition period.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, no - Alex left school quite a while ago now, more than 20 weeks. They've been working for several months already.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying. Let me navigate to the next step based on this information.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**The Rule:** Child Benefit can be claimed for:
- Children under 16, OR
- Children aged 16-19 who are in **approved full-time education or training** (such as school, college, university, or an apprenticeship)

**Your Situation:** 
- Alex is 17 and left school more than 20 weeks ago
- Alex is now working full-time and is not in any approved education or training
- This means Alex no longer qualifies as a "qualifying child" for Child Benefit purposes

**Important Note:** There is a transitional rule that allows a 20-week grace period after leaving education if the young person registers with a careers service or the armed forces, but since Alex left school several months ago (beyond 20 weeks), this extension period has also expired.

**What happens next:**
- You cannot claim Child Benefit for Alex at this time
- If Alex's circumstances change and they re-enter full-time education or training before age 20, you may be able to claim again

If you have any other children you'd like me to assess, I'd be happy to help with those as well!

Let me now record this outcome formally:
